evidence: curier.mapper.ts: CurierMapper.mapToDomain and CurierMapper.mapToOrm are the only places that translate between ORM and domain entities, including the inline OrderEntity/OrderOrmEntity mapping.

curier.repository.ts: CurierRepository implements CreateCurierOutPort, FindAllCuriersOutPort, FindCurierByIdWithOrdersOutPort, SaveCurierOutPort, FindCurierOrderLadingOutPort and FindCountOfFreeCuriersOutPort, all for courier persistence.
curier.repository.ts: findCurierOrderLading, createCurier, findAllCuriers, findCurierByIdWithOrders and save all return their results through CurierMapper, so the mapper is never bypassed.
curier.repository.ts: createCurier and save have the same body (mapToOrm -> curierRepository.save -> mapToDomain). This is minor duplication, not a duplicated domain invariant.

curier.repository.ts: findCurierByIdWithOrders filters orders with isActive: true through ordersRepository, while findCurierOrderLading joins orders with no such filter. This is an inconsistency, but the rule is not stated in two places.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files form one persistence unit for the courier aggregate. curier.mapper.ts (CurierMapper) translates between CurierOrmEntity/OrderOrmEntity and CurierEntity/OrderEntity. curier.repository.ts (CurierRepository) implements the six courier outbound ports on top of TypeORM. Every repository method that returns a domain object uses CurierMapper.mapToDomain, and every write uses CurierMapper.mapToOrm, so the module's own mapping abstraction is never bypassed. The field-by-field mapping, including how orders are mapped, lives only in CurierMapper. Minor issues that do not break cohesion: (1) createCurier and save have the same body; (2) the order mapping is written inline in CurierMapper rather than in its own mapper; (3) orders are loaded two different ways. findCurierByIdWithOrders filters on isActive through a separate ordersRepository, while findCurierOrderLading uses a join with no isActive filter. Possible bug: findAllCuriers calls find() without loading orders, but mapToDomain calls .map on orders, so it may fail at runtime. That is a correctness issue rather than a boundary or cohesion violation.
